  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

The bead is too big when any of these holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate top-level deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across more than ~5 files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass and favor child-bead scoping before implementation.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children may split once more, and third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (focused title, description, AC; copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'` so the decomposition is visible.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260508T205324-8992c1f5/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing each child ID and slice, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a successful attempt. Do not mix partial implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260508T205324-8992c1f5/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

If you write `.ddx/executions/20260508T205324-8992c1f5/no_changes_rationale.txt`, it MUST carry one of:

- `verification_command: <one-line shell command>` — the loop runs it (cwd = project root, 60s); exit 0 closes the bead, non-zero rejects.
- `status: needs_investigation` + `reason: <why>` — bead stays open for triage.

Bare rationales ("nothing to do") are rejected.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260508T205324-8992c1f5/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260508T205324-8992c1f5/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Bead overrides project defaults

The bead description and AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and conservative project defaults (YAGNI, DOWITYTD, no-docs-unless-asked) in this worktree — write whatever the bead asks for.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-b633cbb3">
    <title>routing: rename Profile→Policy + soft min/max + drop ModelRef in internal/routing</title>
    <description>
PROBLEM
  internal/routing engine carries legacy Profile field naming, treats MinPower/MaxPower as hard candidate filters, threads a ModelRef field the v0.11 surface no longer uses, and resolves catalog refs through Inputs.CatalogResolver callbacks the service layer no longer needs. ErrNoLiveProvider.StartingTier is a field-name bug — it always held the policy name.

ROOT CAUSE
  Engine predates the v0.11 routing-surface redesign. "Profile" was the canonical routing input, "model-ref" was a kitchen-sink string accepting policies/targets/aliases, and power bounds were enforced as exclusion gates rather than scoring signals.

DESIGN INTENT (v0.11)
  - "Policy" is the single canonical word for the named routing-intent bundle. No aliases.
  - ModelRef removed; callers pass concrete req.Model when pinning, otherwise rely on req.Policy.
  - MinPower/MaxPower preserved on the request but become asymmetric scoring weights, NOT filters. Undershoot 5x worse than overshoot: power_score = -5*max(0, min_power - cand.power) - 1*max(0, cand.power - max_power).
  - New per-policy bool req.AllowLocal controls whether local-billing candidates are included. Smart's allow_local=false produces fail-closed when subscription is dry (no candidates → ErrNoLiveProvider).
  - require[] is a list of hard-constraint predicates applied as candidate filter. v0.11 ships with one: "no_remote" (cand.DeploymentClass == "local").
  - Pin-pin conflicts (harness×model, harness×provider, provider×model) fail with ErrUnsatisfiablePin BEFORE scoring.

CURRENT STATE WITH FILE:LINE
  - internal/routing/engine.go:16-34 Request struct: Profile, ModelRef, MinPower/MaxPower fields
  - internal/routing/engine.go:284-308 ErrNoLiveProvider.StartingTier (field-name bug)
  - internal/routing/engine.go:305 ProfileEscalationLadder
  - internal/routing/engine.go:1175-1209 ModelRef-driven catalog resolution branch
  - internal/routing/engine.go:1229-1257 EscalateProfileAware
  - internal/routing/errors.go:11-15,46-98 errProfilePinConflict, errNoProfileCandidate sentinels
  - internal/routing/score.go:28,36,58-101 scorePolicy switch on profile name strings
  - internal/routing/gating.go pin-collision predicates

PROPOSED FIX
  1. Rename Request.Profile → Request.Policy. Add Request.AllowLocal bool, Request.Require []string. Drop Request.ModelRef.
  2. Add asymmetric soft-power scoring in score.go (formula above).
  3. Add pin-pin compatibility predicate in gating.go. Apply Require[] predicates as candidate filter. Only "no_remote" defined in v0.11.
  4. Delete Inputs.CatalogResolver and Inputs.CatalogCandidatesResolver fields. Drop the ModelRef branch in resolveModel (engine.go:1175-1209).
  5. errors.go: replace ErrProfilePinConflict, ErrNoProfileCandidate with single ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied{Policy, Requirement, AttemptedPin string, Rejected int}. Add ErrUnknownPolicy{Policy string}, ErrUnsatisfiablePin{Pin, Reason string}.
  6. Rename ErrNoLiveProvider.StartingTier → StartingPolicy. Rename ProfileEscalationLadder → PolicyEscalationLadder; values ["cheap", "default", "smart"].
  7. Rename EscalateProfileAware → EscalatePolicyAware. Internal helpers: missingProfileCapability → missingPolicyCapability; explicitProfileConstraint → explicitPolicyConstraint; harnessViolatesProfileConstraint, modelPinViolatesProfileConstraint similarly.
  8. score.go switch cases canonicalized: "cheap" / "default" / "smart". Format strings "profile=%s" → "policy=%s".

NON-SCOPE
  - Public service surface (service*.go) — Phase 4.
  - Catalog manifest schema — Phase 2.
  - CLI flags — Phase 6.
  - DDx coordination — Phase 9.

PARENT + DEPS
  Leads phase chain. Phase 2 depends on this.
  9. ErrNoLiveProvider enhancement: in addition to renaming StartingTier→StartingPolicy, add RejectedCandidates []CandidateRejection field. CandidateRejection carries {Provider, Harness, Model string, Reason string} where Reason is a typed enum-string ("quota_exhausted", "unhealthy", "model_unavailable", "harness_unhealthy", "policy_filtered"). Update ErrNoLiveProvider.Error() to surface rejection counts when len(RejectedCandidates) > 0:
     - empty rejected list: "no candidates match policy %q (power %d-%d, allow_local=%v); check policy fit and provider configuration"
     - non-empty: "policy %q has %d candidate(s) matching power %d-%d but all rejected: %d quota-exhausted, %d unhealthy, %d unavailable"
     This addresses the operator-visible error language gap raised by fizeau-0d15ab58 (DDx pre-claim readiness): today `no live provider supports prompt of 0 tokens at tier >= smart` collapses two distinct operator scenarios (no smart route exists vs all smart routes are quota-dry); after this change the message tells the operator which bucket they're in.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. internal/routing/policy_test.go::TestPolicyRequireNoRemoteFiltersRemoteCandidates passes (req.Require=["no_remote"] with mixed local+remote candidate set returns only local).
2. internal/routing/policy_test.go::TestPolicyRequireBlocksRemotePinConflict passes (req.Require=["no_remote"] + req.Provider="openrouter" returns ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied{Policy, Requirement:"no_remote", AttemptedPin:"openrouter"}).
3. internal/routing/score_power_test.go::TestSoftPowerScoring_Power9BeatsPower7WhenHealthy passes.
4. internal/routing/score_power_test.go::TestSoftPowerScoring_AsymmetricUndershootHeavier passes (power-7 candidate beats power-11 candidate when both healthy and equal cost given req.MinPower=8/MaxPower=10 — verifies 5:1 undershoot:overshoot ratio).
5. internal/routing/gating_test.go::TestPinPinConflictHarnessIncompatibleWithModel passes (Harness=claude+Model=qwen3.6 returns ErrUnsatisfiablePin{Pin:"harness=claude+model=qwen3.6", Reason}).
6. internal/routing/score_subscription_test.go::TestSubscriptionPreferenceFavorsHighestHeadroom passes (verifies existing subscription-quota wiring populates the scorer).
7. internal/routing/policy_test.go::TestAllowLocalFalseExcludesLocalCandidates passes (req.AllowLocal=false drops all DeploymentClass==local candidates from the pool).
8. grep -rn "Profile\b" internal/routing/*.go (excluding _test.go) returns zero matches outside go-stdlib `errors.Is(target error)` patterns.
9. grep -rn "ModelRef" internal/routing/ returns zero matches.
10. grep -rn "CatalogResolver\|CatalogCandidatesResolver" internal/routing/ returns zero matches.
11. cd /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau && go test ./internal/routing/... -count=1 green.
12. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
13. internal/routing/errors_test.go::TestErrNoLiveProviderDistinguishesEmptyVsAllUnhealthy passes — given 3 candidates that match policy "smart" power range but all return quota_exhausted health status, ErrNoLiveProvider.Error() includes substring "3 candidate(s)" and "quota-exhausted"; given zero matching candidates (empty pool after policy filter), ErrNoLiveProvider.Error() includes substring "no candidates match policy" and "power 9-10".
14. internal/routing/engine.go ErrNoLiveProvider struct has fields: StartingPolicy string, RejectedCandidates []CandidateRejection. CandidateRejection type defined with Provider, Harness, Model, Reason fields.
    </acceptance>
